reviews.title: Lebara left me without service for 11 days after I reported suspected fraud—then ignored me until I went to the Ombudsman
reviews.body:
Lebara left me without service for 11 days after I reported suspected fraud—then ignored me until I went to the Ombudsman

I received repeated verification codes linked to attempts to move my number to another SIM. Two £30 payment attempts were declined, then three £5 top-ups were taken using the card saved on my account. I had never bought PAYG vouchers. I reported the activity to my bank and Lebara, but after the bank reclaimed the disputed payments, Lebara barred my service.

Lebara told me to reverse the chargeback or pay £15 by voucher. It asked me for a police report, which I provided, but still refused to restore my service at that point. It has never clearly explained what investigation it carried out, whether it checked the activity against my normal account use, or what security steps it took. Instead, it repeatedly focused on its own “financial loss.”

The 11-day outage had serious consequences. I’m a community nurse and rely on my phone for work and travel. I also care for disabled relatives. I told Lebara my mother had fallen and I couldn’t contact her carers, but it maintained its position. I also struggled with medical appointments and calls about credit-card payments.

I sent more than 50 emails. Many were ignored or met with generic replies; promised call backs never came and stated timescales were missed. I contacted senior staff and posted Trustpilot reviews, but received no personal response until I opened an Ombudsman case. After that, Lebara began calling repeatedly to ask why I was leaving—and asked me to delete my reviews.

 It also promised my Deadlock Letter by 21 October after I had been chasing it for months. The deadline passed and I’m still waiting, I am concerned that this is a deliberate attempt to hinder the Ombudsman investigation.

Lebara has found time to ask why I’m leaving and to ask me to remove my reviews, but still hasn’t provided the letter it promised or answered my concerns. My complaint is with the Communications Ombudsman. This has been an exhausting and deeply disappointing customer experience.

reviews.title: Bought a refurbished iPhone for my…
reviews.body:
Bought a refurbished iPhone for my daughter who is now walking to and from school alone. The website states that all their refurbished phones come with minimum 80% battery health.

Phone was posted quickly and daughter started using the same day. That night I thought to check the battery health and it was 76% and there was a message saying the battery health is ‘significantly degraded’. 

Contacted Lebara and their customer service was very quick. They were offering for me to send the phone back to check and replace but with a 10 working day turnaround time. They were insistent on this until I stated that the Consumer Rights act states that timeframes must be reasonable and not put a customer at significant inconvenience, which 10 working days would, as my daughter would be walking to/from school alone with no phone for potentially 2 weeks. 

They agreed to a quicker turnaround so we were only without a phone for 2 days which was good. 

Unfortunately - the second phone also arrived with a ‘significantly degraded’ battery at 79%. 

Contacted them again and I was offered a refund or to return the phone for replacement again.

At this point it is very frustrating as my daughter now needs this phone. 

I asked for a partial refund which they agreed to and took 5 working days to receive. 

I have given 2 stars because customer service were responsive and helpful (once threatened with trading standards) but ultimately I am still with a phone that does not have the battery health promised so I am not happy about that. It does have a 12 month warranty so we’ll see.
